identity.operation: Parse a four-component OBJ v line and publish vertex_weights.
identity.condition: A v line has a fourth component.
identity.capability: Retain the fourth component in vertex_weights and transfer it to output attributes.
identity.consequence: The vertex weight is missing or incorrect.

requirement: For a four-component v line, retain the fourth component as a vertex weight.

assessment.necessity_reason: A finite input with a four-component OBJ v line, followed by the harness’s NUL delimiter, reaches the new parser path and publishes the fourth component in vertex_weights.

before.requirement: Publish the fourth component of a v line as a dedicated vertex weight.
before.reason: The before parser has no separate weight accumulator. Its output path swaps the vertex vector before using that same vector for vertex_weights, so this capability is absent on the before side.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The output path empties v into vertices before swapping v into vertex_weights.
ParseFromString passes the OBJ text to this LoadObj overload.

after.requirement: For a four-component OBJ v line, retain the fourth component as a vertex weight and publish it in the output attributes.
after.reason: The changed helper returns four components when only one value follows xyz. LoadObj appends that value to vertex_weights and transfers the vector to the output attributes. The harness can provide the line as OBJ text before its delimiter.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The helper distinguishes a fourth component from a complete RGB triple.
LoadObj transfers the accumulated vertex weights to the output attributes.
ParseFromString passes the supplied OBJ text to this LoadObj overload.

assessment.comparison_reason: The dedicated vertex-weight behavior is absent before the change and reachable afterward using the same old harness.

necessity_evidence.reason: The old harness can pass a four-component OBJ vertex line to ParseFromString. The after parser retains its fourth value in vertex_weights and publishes it, so the claimed coverage gap has a direct equivalent route.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: Input bytes: "v 1 2 3 0.5\n\0x". The bytes before NUL are OBJ text; "x" is MTL text.

scope_contract.reason: ParseFromString passes the harness-supplied OBJ text to LoadObj, whose vertex parser handles v lines.

evidence.dependency_reason: Connects ParseFromString to the LoadObj vertex parser.
Shows the entry passes the OBJ text to ParseFromString.

feasible_trigger.reason: The witness supplies a valid four-component v line, but the harness routes it to the parser; the claimed blocked setup does not exist.

evidence.dependency_reason: A NUL delimiter makes the preceding bytes OBJ text and invokes ParseFromString.
Passes that OBJ text to LoadObj.

observable_consequence.reason: For four components, the helper returns 4 with the fourth value in r; LoadObj appends r to vertex_weights and transfers that vector to the output attributes.

evidence.dependency_reason: The harness can invoke this path with the witness bytes.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The candidate's own counterevidence is decisive: the existing NUL split and ParseFromString call provide a direct route to the four-component parser and output transfer.

evidence.dependency_reason: Routes the OBJ text into LoadObj.
Transfers the reached weight value to output attributes.

identity_preserved.reason: The same tuple—four-component v line, fourth-component weight, published vertex_weights—is assessed on both versions with the same old harness. The before parser has no separate weight accumulator; the after parser does, and the harness reaches it.

evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the before output path uses the already-swapped vertex vector for vertex_weights.
Shows the after output path publishes the separate weight vector.
The fixed harness used for both assessments.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Connects the entry operation to LoadObj.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Retain the fourth component of a four-component OBJ v line in vertex_weights.
coverage_witness.required_setup: Pass an OBJ string containing a four-component v line to ParseFromString.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: The harness splits input at the first eligible NUL byte and passes the prefix as OBJ text to ParseFromString.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: None; the frozen candidate's behavior is reachable.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: The harness's existing NUL split and ParseFromString call directly reach the LoadObj vertex parser and its vertex_weights output transfer.
